questions.question: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in:
questions.explanation: The United Nations headquarters is located in New York City, USA, on international territory. Other major UN offices are in Geneva, Vienna, and Nairobi.

questions.question: Which organization is known as the 'lender of last resort' for developing countries?
questions.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) acts as a lender of last resort, providing financial assistance to member countries facing balance of payment crises with conditional reforms.

questions.question: INTERPOL headquarters is located in:
questions.explanation: INTERPOL (International Criminal Police Organization) is headquartered in Lyon, France. It facilitates international police cooperation among 195 member countries.

questions.question: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) was established after which nuclear test?
questions.explanation: NSG was established in 1974 as a direct response to India's first nuclear test 'Smiling Buddha' (Pokhran-I) to prevent proliferation of nuclear weapons technology.

questions.question: The ASEAN Secretariat is based in which city?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat is headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia. ASEAN was founded in 1967 and currently has 10 member states in Southeast Asia.

questions.question: Which UN agency deals with civil aviation standards and regulations?
questions.explanation: ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organization) is a specialized UN agency that sets global standards for civil aviation safety, security, efficiency and environmental protection.

questions.question: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) was established by:
questions.explanation: FATF was established in 1989 by the G7 Summit in Paris to combat money laundering and terrorist financing. India became a member in 2010.

questions.question: The International Energy Agency (IEA) was founded as a response to which crisis?
questions.explanation: IEA was founded in 1974 as a response to the 1973 Arab oil embargo, to coordinate energy policies of member countries and provide reliable energy data.

questions.question: India is a founding member of which of the following organizations?
questions.explanation: India is a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), established in 1961 in Belgrade. India co-founded it with Yugoslavia, Egypt, Ghana, and Indonesia.

questions.question: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) was adopted in which year?
questions.explanation: The CTBT was adopted by the UN General Assembly in September 1996. However, it has not yet entered into force as key states including USA, China, India, Pakistan have not ratified it.

questions.question: Which institution publishes the 'World Economic Outlook' report?
questions.explanation: The World Economic Outlook (WEO) is a flagship publication of the IMF, released twice a year, providing forecasts and analysis of the global economy.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the UN. Where is it located?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is located at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. It settles disputes between states and gives advisory opinions on legal questions.
